> load(file="LDSCoutputCogNonCog.RData")
> 
> 
> model<-'C=~NA*EA + start(0.4)*CP
+         NC=~NA*EA
+          
+          NC~~1*NC
+          C~~1*C
+          C~~0*NC
+ 
+          CP ~~ 0*EA
+          CP~~0*CP
+          EA~~0*EA'
> 
> 
> output<-usermodel(LDSCoutput,estimation="DWLS",model=model)
[1] "Running primary model"
[1] "Calculating CFI"
[1] "Calculating Standardized Results"
[1] "Calculating SRMR"
elapsed

[1] "Model fit statistics are all printed as NA as you have specified a fully saturated model (i.e., df = 0)"
> 

I am not sure why it came up as a fully saturated model instead of results resembling the example.  I would appreciate any help in this - when I ran my own model I also came up with fully saturated (SCZ-Smoking).  V/R Dan
